correctness.rationale: Read frozen RESULT.md. Poisson-kernel cosine integral with a=mr²+2k and b=2k yields lambda(r)=(sqrt(r²+4k/m)-r)/(sqrt(r²+4k/m)+r), C_d/K=sum lambda_i^(d+1)/(1-lambda_i²). Substitute lambda=tanh(theta/2): s=(sinh theta1+sinh theta2)/2,1+t=(cosh theta1+cosh theta2)/2. Mean/difference angles c,h imply s=sinh(c)cosh(h),1+t=cosh(c)cosh(h); positivity c>h gives 0<=h<asinh(2s)/2 and exactly the sharp lower closed, upper open t-boundary. Every feasible observation fixes c,h up to permutation. One s leaves a continuum of theta pairs. This proof covers all finite positive rates at known parameters; it does not prove finite-chain inference.
